mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of consecutive GDP declines, or the mechanism fails in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1, quarterly, interpolated monthly) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 (interpolated monthly) and HOUST both decline in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to produce a statistically significant negative median return.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% combined with a concurrent decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% signals a deflationary easing cycle, which increases risk appetite and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails in more than 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 persons per month for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 200000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not above the baseline at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% YoY while personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1, interpolated monthly) are flat or declining signals a precautionary savings regime, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > 5% AND GDPC1 (interpolated monthly) is flat or declining in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails in more than 50% of such instances.
